experiment_data.hypothesis: F-L scalar correction (tau_obs/(1-2*pi_bar)) predicts bias direction incorrectly under subgroup heterogeneity because it uses a single global scaling factor that over-corrects low-error subgroups and under-corrects high-error subgroups. EC-HTE's CM inversion handles the sign-reversal correctly.

metrics.sign_reversal: F-L Scalar: s0=+0.073 s1=+0.068, both positive (no sign-reversal). F-L Per-Subgroup: s0=+0.024 s1=+0.160. EC-HTE: s0=+0.006 s1=+0.001 (near-zero bias both subgroups)
metrics.key_finding: F-L scalar and F-L per-subgroup both WORSE than naive on aggregate |bias|. F-L scalar over-corrects s0 (bias +0.073 vs naive +0.005). F-L per-subgroup dramatically over-corrects s1 (bias +0.160). EC-HTE achieves near-zero per-subgroup bias with nominal coverage (95.3%). CM inversion fundamentally different from F-L scalar rescaling.
